tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

def active?(_), do: false
  def terminal?(%{status: status}), do: status in Status.terminal()
  def terminal?(_), do: false

  @doc "Transition to `:processing`."
  def start(task), do: transition(task, :processing, %{})

  @doc """
  Transition to `:completed`. Optional extra attrs (e.g. `book_id`).
  Broadcasts `{:task_updated, task}` on the task's PubSub topics.
  """
  def complete(task, extra \\ %{}) do
    with {:ok, task} <- transition(task, :completed, extra) do
      broadcast(task)
      {:ok, task}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Transition to `:failed` with a human-readable reason.
  Broadcasts `{:task_updated, task}` on the task's PubSub topics.
  """
  def fail(task, reason) when is_binary(reason) do
    with {:ok, task} <- transition(task, :failed, %{error_message: reason}) do
      broadcast(task)
      {:ok, task}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Subscribe the calling process to every task lifecycle topic. Use from
  LiveViews that refresh on any task transition.
  """
  def subscribe do
    for topic <- @subscribe_topics do
      Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(ReadaloudWeb.PubSub, topic)

It's live: the new voice is now generating Reverend Insanity from your chapter onward.

**Merge and deploy:**
- The work is merged into readaloud's `master`, pushed, and deployed to pylon.
- Readaloud now reads a chapter from its plan (each passage with its own clip of the narrator, names respelled) whenever the chapter has one. Chapters without a plan sound exactly as before.
- Your book's voice setting didn't need to change.

**Where your chapters are:**
- **Chapter 960** (readaloud 211) is done. I checked the audio file and the word timings. The translator/editor header line is no longer read aloud, so highlighting skips those few words.
- **Chapter 961** is generating now.
- **Chapter 959**, the one you're on, failed on its first try and is queued to retry after 961. The failure was my mistake: the planner loaded a model onto the GPU that Breeze uses and crowded it out. The planner now runs off both GPUs. The chapter's old audio was untouched.
- Generation takes about 10 minutes a chapter, and planning about 4–7 minutes, so planning stays ahead.

**The first batch of 100 chapters (959 onward) is running in the background:**
- It should take about 8–10 hours to plan, and the audio will trail behind it.
- New names are respelled as they appear (e.g. "Bai Ning Bing" → "Bye Ning Bing"), and characters keep the same voice across chapters.
- The gameassets tagger is paused while it runs. When the batch finishes, bonsai stops and the tagger timers restart on their own.

**Problems found and fixed along the way:**
- **Wordless chunks.** A chunk with no words could have failed a whole chapter on every retry.
- **Single-word names.** Learned single-word names like "Long" or "Men" could have changed ordinary words in later chapters.
- **Truncated names reply.** One chapter (962) failed when bonsai's names reply ran too long; I fixed that and it's being re-planned.
- **Readaloud's tests.** I fixed two causes of flaky tests in readaloud. One flaky "Database busy" failure predates this work and is still there.

Smaller review notes I left alone:
- A bad chapter ID in the new API returns a 500 instead of a 404.
- An existing plan isn't refreshed if a chapter's text is edited.
- Some HTML tags Reverend Insanity doesn't use could run words together.

Should I start the remaining ~1,275 chapters automatically when this batch ends? That would keep the tagger paused for roughly 4 more days. The other option is to run them in chunks, with the tagger back on in between.

#!/bin/bash
# Plans every Reverend Insanity chapter from readaloud number 210 that has no voice plan yet, then exits.
# Resumable: started by voicerefs-plan.timer after each boot and an hour after a run that left chapters unplanned.
# bonsai-text and the gameassets tagger can't share GPU 1, so the tagger is paused while this runs;
# the service's ExecStopPost always hands the GPU back (voicerefs-plan-release).
set -u
LOG=/internalmedia/voice-refs-work/plan-run-2.log
API=http://pylon:4000/api/books/12/chapters
remaining() {
  curl -sf "$API" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(sum(1 for c in json.load(sys.stdin)["chapters"] if c["number"] >= 210 and not c["voice_plan"]))'
}
before=$(remaining) || { echo "$(date -Is) readaloud unreachable; retrying later" >> "$LOG"; exit 0; }
echo "$(date -Is) start: $before chapters without a plan" >> "$LOG"
if [ "$before" = 0 ]; then systemctl --user disable --now voicerefs-plan.timer; exit 0; fi

systemctl --user stop gameassets-tagger-gpu0.timer gameassets-tagger-gpu1.timer
# Let a tagger run that is already going finish rather than kill its Bonsai.
while systemctl --user is-active -q gameassets-tagger-gpu0.service gameassets-tagger-gpu1.service; do sleep 60; done
systemctl --user start bonsai-text
for _ in $(seq 1 100); do curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:18120/health >/dev/null && break; sleep 3; done

cd /home/noah/projects/readaloud/tools/voice-refs
# No GPU for this process: laya on GPU 0 starves LocalAI's Breeze, and GPU 1 is bonsai's.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" /home/noah/.local/bin/uv run voicerefs plan --start 210 --count 5000 2>&1 \
  | grep --line-buffered -v -E "Warning|warn\(|Fetching|return Agent" >> "$LOG"

after=$(remaining) || after=$before
echo "$(date -Is) end: $after chapters without a plan" >> "$LOG"
if [ "$after" = 0 ]; then
  echo "$(date -Is) all chapters planned; timer disabled" >> "$LOG"
  systemctl --user disable voicerefs-plan.timer
elif [ "$after" -ge "$before" ]; then
  echo "$(date -Is) no progress this run; timer disabled, needs a look" >> "$LOG"
  systemctl --user disable voicerefs-plan.timer
fi
EOF
cat > /internalmedia/voice-refs-work/plan-release.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Hands GPU 1 back to the gameassets tagger after a voicerefs plan run, however it ended.
systemctl --user stop bonsai-text
systemctl --user start gameassets-tagger-gpu0.timer gameassets-tagger-gpu1.timer
EOF
chmod +x /internalmedia/voice-refs-work/plan-rest.sh /internalmedia/voice-refs-work/plan-release.sh
cat > ~/.config/systemd/user/voicerefs-plan.service <<'EOF'
# Temporary (Oct 2026): voice plans for readaloud's Reverend Insanity, see
# ~/projects/readaloud/tools/voice-refs. Remove with the timer once the log says all chapters are planned.
[Unit]
Description=Plan Reverend Insanity chapters for readaloud's matched narrator voice

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/internalmedia/voice-refs-work/plan-rest.sh
ExecStopPost=/internalmedia/voice-refs-work/plan-release.sh
TimeoutStartSec=infinity
Nice=10
EOF
cat > ~/.config/systemd/user/voicerefs-plan.timer <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Resume readaloud voice planning after boot and after unfinished runs

[Timer]
OnBootSec=15min
OnUnitInactiveSec=1h

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF
systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemd-analyze --user verify ~/.config/systemd/user/voicerefs-plan.service ~/.config/systemd/user/voicerefs-plan.timer && echo verified

---
name: readaloud-voice-refs
description: "Matched-reference voice for readaloud's breeze/heath-miller (Oct 2026) — merged + deployed as per-chapter voice plans; how to run the planner, what it pauses, Noah's verdicts"
metadata:
  node_type: memory

Oct 24 2026: fixed breeze-tts-2/heath-miller giving female characters a brutish male voice by giving each passage its own clip of the narrator. Comparison page: https://claude.ai/artifact/SkYqTpnZiJ3hnk7yCnZbpe (RI ch. 944 = readaloud book 12 number 195). Noah approved v2 and asked for it on Reverend Insanity from his chapter on.

**Live since 2026-10-24 (readaloud 3676bb0, merged to master, deployed to pylon):**
- A chapter's *voice plan* (`/var/lib/readaloud/data/files/books/<book>/voice-plans/NNNN.json`) lists chunks with book `text`, `spoken` (respelled names), clip path + transcript, temperature 0.6. GenerateJob uses it when the plan's model/voice match the task; otherwise reads as before. Book voice stays `heath-miller` — plan presence is what switches a chapter.

content.text:
The service is only there because phanteks reboots every day at 05:00. Pausing the tagger and running the planner once would last until that night: the reboot kills the planner, bonsai doesn't come back, and the tagger timers start again since they're enabled at boot. The service just restarts the run after each boot. It's a stopgap for a 4–5 day backfill.

Building it into readaloud is the better design if you want this for every book. It isn't a quick move, though, for three reasons:

- **The models can't run where readaloud runs.** Readaloud is on pylon, which has no GPU. Bonsai is a custom llama.cpp build on phanteks that only listens locally, and LocalAI can't load its ternary quant. Laya and the narrator clip library are Python and data on phanteks too. So readaloud can't do the tagging itself; it can only ask phanteks to.
- **The logic is Python.** The tagging, voice picking, pinyin respelling and passage building are all in the voice-refs tool. Porting them to Elixir would be a rewrite, and laya would still need Python.
- **The GPU conflict doesn't go away.** Bonsai and the tagger can't share GPU 1. Built in or not, planning means pausing the tagger, unless bonsai moves to a GPU the tagger doesn't use.

How I'd integrate it:
- Run the planner as a small always-on HTTP service on phanteks: "plan this chapter".
- `GenerateJob` calls it before synthesizing. A chapter with no plan gets one on demand, and if the planner is down it falls back to the single clip.
- New chapters and new books then get matched voices automatically, in reading order, with readaloud as the only queue. There's no backfill run and nothing to babysit across reboots.
- The cost is that bonsai is resident whenever readaloud generates, so the tagger would need a different GPU, or to only run while readaloud's queue is empty.

Reverend Insanity is a finished book, so the current run will finish it either way. Should I build the on-demand version for future books once this backfill is done? It's worth deciding first where the tagger lives if bonsai stays resident.

content.text:
You're right. I overstated both points.

**Laya:** it doesn't even need porting. Its only job in the pipeline is to mark narration as "action". Bonsai already tags every unit with a mood that includes "action", and the narration voice is chosen by bonsai's cluster pick anyway. So the simplest move is to drop laya. If a check on a few chapters showed it mattered, ONNX through Ortex would be the next step. That also lets the planner use no GPU at all.

**The models can't run where readaloud runs:** that isn't a real blocker. Readaloud already calls LocalAI over HTTP for TTS and Whisper, and it can call bonsai the same way. Bonsai's llama-server is OpenAI-compatible; it just needs to listen beyond localhost, ideally registered in LiteLLM like the other non-Claude models.

**The logic is Python:** the per-chapter part ports to Elixir without much trouble. That's the quote and passage splitting, pinyin respelling, the bonsai prompts and schemas, the voice-group rules and the speaker memory. The narrator voice library is static data: the clips are already in LocalAI's voices folder, and their labels sit in `clusters.json` and `library.json`. Only building a library for a new narrator (clustering the audiobook) stays an offline Python tool.

What I'd build:
1. **`ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner` in Elixir.** It tags the chapter through bonsai, picks a clip per passage, and respells names, producing the same plan format as now.
2. **Planning inside `GenerateJob`.** A chapter with no plan gets one first; if bonsai is unreachable, it falls back to the single clip. Names learned and per-character voices are stored in readaloud's DB, per book.
3. **Narrator library as data.** It's loaded from a JSON file checked into the repo, so the Python tool exports it and readaloud reads it.
4. **Bonsai reachable from pylon.** This is a configs change: bind it beyond localhost and add a LiteLLM model entry. Bonsai stays resident on GPU 1, and the tagger is yours to manage.

The current backfill keeps running in the meantime. Its plans use the same format, so nothing it makes is wasted. Once this lands, the service becomes unnecessary and I remove it.

One thing to confirm before I start: keep bonsai as the tagging model, since it produced the results you approved? The alternative is a LocalAI-served model, which LocalAI can load on demand but which would need re-checking against the comparison page.

Right, and that's the clean answer: give bonsai a GPU of its own instead of pausing the tagger. Here's what's actually on the cards right now, though:

- **GPU 0:** LocalAI, holding Breeze and Whisper. That's about 10 GB of 12, and readaloud's TTS lives here.
- **GPU 1:** bonsai, 8.3 GB of 12.
- **Tagger:** set up to run on both GPUs, with one ternary Bonsai server per GPU (`bonsai.gpus = ["0" "1"]`).

So there's no free GPU for a second resident bonsai. Bonsai can't fit beside LocalAI on GPU 0, and on GPU 1 the tagger's server and the text server can't both be resident.

However, the tagger's vision server and the planner's text server load the same model file, `Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B`; the tagger's just adds the vision projector. That makes a layout with no conflict at all:

- **GPU 1:** one resident Bonsai server, vision projector included, serving both the tagger and readaloud's planner. It runs with two parallel slots so neither waits on the other's long requests.
- **GPU 0:** LocalAI alone. The tagger's GPU 0 shard goes away; it was squeezing LocalAI anyway, the same way laya did today.

def _ensure_up(
    client: BonsaiClient,
    settings: Settings,
    systemctl: Callable[[list[str]], str],
    sleep: Callable[[float], None],
    clock: Callable[[], float],
    guard: Callable[[], bool],
) -> str:
    """ "up", "timeout", or "yield" (canon wants the GPU while we wait for the model)."""
    if client.healthy():
        return "up"
    systemctl(["start", settings.bonsai_unit])
    deadline = clock() + START_TIMEOUT_S
    while clock() < deadline:
        if guard():
            return "yield"
        if client.healthy():
            return "up"
        sleep(2.0)
    return "timeout"


def _watch(
    guard: Callable[[], bool],
    stop_bonsai: Callable[[], object],
    every: float,
    done: threading.Event,
    yielding: threading.Event,
) -> None:
    """Poll the canon guard until the run ends; on a hit stop Bonsai at once."""
    while not done.wait(every):
        try:
            if guard():
                yielding.set()
                stop_bonsai()
                return
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a failed check is retried next poll
            log.exception("canon guard check failed")


def _on_sigterm(signum, frame):
    raise SystemExit(128 + signum)


def run(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
    settings: Settings,
    *,
    sample: int | None = None,
    report: Path | None = None,
    client: BonsaiClient | None = None,
    guard: Callable[[], bool] | None = None,
    systemctl: Callable[[list[str]], str] = _systemctl,
    notify: Callable[[], None] | None = None,
    sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep,
    clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
    watch_s: float = WATCH_S,
) -> RunStats:
    client = client or BonsaiClient(settings.bonsai_url)
    guard = guard or (lambda: canon_active(systemctl))
    notify = notify or _notify_scan(settings.port)
    stats = RunStats()
    records: list[_Record] = []
    pending_jobs = _shard_jobs(conn, settings)
    pending_items = sum(len(j.items) for j in pending_jobs)
    sampled = round_robin(pending_jobs, sample) if sample is not None else None
    if not pending_jobs:
        return stats  # nothing to tag: Bonsai is never started (the timer fires hourly)
    begun = clock()
    first_job_at: float | None = None
    up = False
    since_classify = 0
    job_no = 0
    # A SIGTERM from systemd must still reach the finally that stops the Bonsai unit.
    try:
        previous = signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _on_sigterm)
    except ValueError:  # not the main thread
        previous = None
    finished, yielding = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
    watcher = threading.Thread(
        target=_watch,
        args=(
            guard,
            lambda: systemctl(["stop", settings.bonsai_unit]),
            watch_s,
            finished,
            yielding,
        ),
        name="canon-guard",
        daemon=True,
    )
    watcher.start()
    try:
        while True:
            if yielding.is_set() or guard():
                stats.status = "yielded"
                break
            if not up:
                state = _ensure_up(client, settings, systemctl, sleep, clock, guard)
                if state != "up":
                    stats.status = "yielded" if state == "yield" else "bonsai_unavailable"
                    break
                up = True
                stats.cold_start_s = clock() - begun
            if sampled is not None:
                if not sampled:
                    break
                job = sampled.pop(0)
            else:
                batch = _shard_jobs(conn, settings)
                if not batch:
                    break
                job = batch[0]
            if first_job_at is None:
                first_job_at = clock()
            job_no += 1
            try:
                done, failed, parked, recs = _process(conn, settings, client, job, job_no, yielding)
            except (httpx.TransportError, _Yielded) as exc:
                if yielding.is_set() or isinstance(
                    exc, _Yielded
                ):  # the watcher stopped Bonsai for canon: not a failure
                    log.info("canon-llama started; Bonsai stopped mid-call, yielding")
                    stats.status = "yielded"
                    break
                for item in job.items:
                    stats.failed += 1
                    stats.parked += int(_bump_errors(conn, item.shas))
                log.error("Bonsai unreachable: %s", exc)
                stats.status = "bonsai_down"
                break
            stats.done += done
            stats.jobs_done += int(done > 0)
            stats.failed += failed
            stats.parked += parked
            records += recs
            since_classify += 1
            if since_classify >= CLASSIFY_EVERY:
                _retry(conn, types.classify_all, conn, settings)
                since_classify = 0
    finally:
        finished.set()
        watcher.join(timeout=watch_s + 65)  # a systemctl call has a 60 s timeout
        try:
            systemctl(["stop", settings.bonsai_unit])
        finally:
            if first_job_at is not None:
                stats.seconds = clock() - first_job_at
            if stats.seconds > 0:
                stats.per_hour = stats.done / stats.seconds * 3600
                stats.jobs_per_hour = stats.jobs_done / stats.seconds * 3600
            if previous is not None:
                signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, previous)
            if stats.done or since_classify:
                _retry(conn, types.classify_all, conn, settings)
            if report is not None:
                write_report(report, records, stats, pending_items)
            if stats.done:
                notify()
    return stats


def projected_hours(pending_items: int, stats: RunStats) -> float | None:
    """Hours to tag every pending item at the measured items-per-hour rate."""
    return pending_items / stats.per_hour if stats.per_hour else None

# Gameassets — searchable index over the purchased game-asset library
# (FastAPI + SQLite FTS5 + MCP, Python source colocated under svc/ and
# web/), plus the Bonsai vision server and the tagger that feeds it.
#
# Phanteks-only (user scope): the library is the /mnt/bigmedia Samba
# mount and the Bonsai llama.cpp build lives in noah's home. Registered
# as an MCP backend in the LiteLLM gateway
# (nix/services/modules/litellm/config.yaml → http://phanteks:8104/mcp).
#
# Units:
#   gameassets          the service (HTTP + MCP on :8104, scan loop)
#   gameassets-bonsai-gpu<N>
#                       llama.cpp vision server on GPU N, 127.0.0.1:1811N,
#                       one per services.gameassets.bonsai.gpus. No
#                       Install section: its tagger starts and stops it,
#                       and stops it within ~5 s of a canon-llama@* unit
#                       appearing (the two compete for the GPU). The
#                       tagger's ExecStopPost also stops it whenever the
#                       tagger exits for any reason (SIGKILL included).
#                       Starting it by hand pulls in nothing.
#   bonsai-text        llama.cpp text server (no vision) on GPU 1,
#                       127.0.0.1:18120, for the Ψ-RAG canon tree. No
#                       Install section: started and stopped by hand.
#                       Competes with gameassets-bonsai-gpu1 for that
#                       card (~7 GB each of 12): they must not run
#                       together, so it Conflicts= with it (starting
#                       either stops the other). Port 18120 sits
#                       deliberately outside the 1811N vision scheme.
#   gameassets-tagger-gpu<N>
#                       oneshot `tag` run against that GPU's server, on
#                       its shard of the queue; hourly timer only when
#                       services.gameassets.tagger.schedule.enable.
#
# One-time library setup before the first deploy (run by hand with sudo;
# the Samba share creates files as `nobody`, and the organizer, running
# as noah, must be able to move them):
#   sudo setfacl -R -m u:noah:rwX -m d:u:noah:rwX /mnt/bigmedia/media/GameAssets
#   mkdir -p /mnt/bigmedia/media/GameAssets/_inbox
# Verify a file created through the Samba share is movable by noah.
#
# No RequiresMountsFor: a user manager cannot order against system
# mount units. The service tolerates a missing root and rescans.
{
  mkSystemdService,
  pkgs,
nix/services/modules/gameassets/default.nix
nix/services/modules/gameassets/svc/tagger.py
UNIT FILE            STATE  VENDOR PRESET
canon-llama@.service static -

"""Runtime settings, sourced from the environment by the systemd unit."""

from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="GAMEASSETS_")

    # The purchased library. Opened read-only; nothing is ever written here.
    root: Path = Path("/mnt/bigmedia/media/GameAssets")
    # Everything derived (database, thumbnails, reports) lives here.
    state_dir: Path = Path("/home/noah/.local/share/gameassets")
    port: int = 8104
    host: str = "0.0.0.0"
    # How clients reach this service; every URL the API hands out starts with it.
    public_url: str = "http://phanteks:8104"
    # Top-level directories that are never indexed.
    excluded_top: list[str] = ["Tools", "_archives"]
    # Where new packs arrive, and where the organizer parks what it cannot place.
    inbox_dir: str = "_inbox"
    unknown_dir: str = "_Unknown"
    unsorted_dir: str = "_Unsorted"
    superseded_dir: str = "_archives/superseded"
    # The library's own attribution list, relative to root.
    authors_file: str = "README.md"
    # Directory depth below a category that names the pack; categories not
    # listed use depth 1.
    pack_depth: dict[str, int] = {"Sprites": 2}
    # A file modified more recently than this is still being written.
    settle_seconds: int = 120
    scan_interval_s: int = 600
    # False: the loop only plans (organize dry run); nothing moves the library until Noah
    # approves the plan and this is turned on.
    organize_enabled: bool = False
    # An archive that would unpack to more than this is refused (zip bombs).
    max_import_bytes: int = 20 * 1024**3
    # ... or holds more members than this.
    max_import_members: int = 100_000
    # One Bonsai server per GPU, on port 18110 + the GPU's index; each tagger drives one.
    bonsai_url: str = "http://127.0.0.1:18111"
    bonsai_unit: str = "gameassets-bonsai-gpu1.service"
    # With several taggers (one per GPU), each takes the jobs whose lead content hash
    # falls in its shard, so no two of them tag the same thing.
    tagger_shard: int = 0
    tagger_shards: int = 1
    # Human edits are mirrored here so they survive a lost state dir.
    export_path: Path = Path("/mnt/mega/backups/gameassets/edits.json")


@lru_cache
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()

# Resident mode: one Bonsai server on the GPU, shared with other clients (readaloud's
# voice planner), so the tagger neither stops it after a run nor waits for work to start it.
def test_resident_server_left_running_after_a_run(conn, cfg, lib_root):
    _png(lib_root / "Sprites/Props/PackR/rock.png", (80, 80))
    _scan(conn, cfg)
    resident = cfg.model_copy(update={"bonsai_resident": True})
    stats, sysd, _ = _go(conn, resident, Fake())
    assert stats.done == 1
    assert ["stop", cfg.bonsai_unit] not in [c[:2] for c in sysd.calls]


def test_resident_server_brought_back_even_with_an_empty_queue(conn, cfg, lib_root):
    _scan(conn, cfg)
    fake = Fake()
    fake.healthy = False
    resident = cfg.model_copy(update={"bonsai_resident": True})
    stats, sysd, _ = _go(conn, resident, fake, clock=iter(range(0, 10_000, 100)).__next__)
    assert sysd.calls[0][:2] == ["start", cfg.bonsai_unit]
    assert ["stop", cfg.bonsai_unit] not in [c[:2] for c in sysd.calls]

#!/bin/bash
# Plans every Reverend Insanity chapter from readaloud number 210 that has no voice plan yet, then exits.
# Resumable: started by voicerefs-plan.timer after each boot and an hour after a run that left chapters unplanned.
# Uses the resident Bonsai on GPU 1 that the gameassets tagger shares, so nothing is paused.
set -u
LOG=/internalmedia/voice-refs-work/plan-run-2.log
API=http://pylon:4000/api/books/12/chapters
remaining() {
  curl -sf "$API" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(sum(1 for c in json.load(sys.stdin)["chapters"] if c["number"] >= 210 and not c["voice_plan"]))'
}
before=$(remaining) || { echo "$(date -Is) readaloud unreachable; retrying later" >> "$LOG"; exit 0; }
echo "$(date -Is) start: $before chapters without a plan" >> "$LOG"
if [ "$before" = 0 ]; then systemctl --user disable --now voicerefs-plan.timer; exit 0; fi

for _ in $(seq 1 100); do curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:18111/health >/dev/null && break; sleep 3; done

cd /home/noah/projects/readaloud/tools/voice-refs
# No GPU for this process: laya on GPU 0 starves LocalAI's Breeze, and GPU 1 is Bonsai's.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" /home/noah/.local/bin/uv run voicerefs plan --start 210 --count 5000 2>&1 \
  | grep --line-buffered -v -E "Warning|warn\(|Fetching|return Agent" >> "$LOG"

after=$(remaining) || after=$before
echo "$(date -Is) end: $after chapters without a plan" >> "$LOG"
if [ "$after" = 0 ]; then
  echo "$(date -Is) all chapters planned; timer disabled" >> "$LOG"
  systemctl --user disable voicerefs-plan.timer
elif [ "$after" -ge "$before" ]; then
  echo "$(date -Is) no progress this run; timer disabled, needs a look" >> "$LOG"
  systemctl --user disable voicerefs-plan.timer
fi

defmodule ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.ParityTest do
  # The planner was first written in Python (tools/voice-refs) and its output was what
  # Noah approved; test/fixtures/planner_parity.json is that code's output on the same
  # inputs (regenerate with tools/voice-refs/explore/parity_fixture.py).
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true

  alias ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.{Names, Text}

  @fixture "test/fixtures/planner_parity.json" |> File.read!() |> Jason.decode!()

  test "pinyin names are respelled exactly as the Python planner respells them" do
    for {name, expected} <- @fixture["respell"] do
      assert {name, Names.respell(name)} == {name, expected}
    end
  end

  test "names and word fixes are substituted exactly as in Python" do
    for %{"text" => text, "map" => map, "out" => out} <- @fixture["apply_names"] do
      assert Names.apply(text, map) == out
    end
  end

  test "chapter HTML splits into the same paragraphs and quote units" do
    for %{"html" => html, "paragraphs" => paragraphs, "units" => units} <- @fixture["html"] do
      assert Text.paragraphs(html) == paragraphs

      assert paragraphs |> Text.units() |> Enum.map(&Map.take(&1, [:para, :text, :quoted])) ==
               Enum.map(units, fn u -> %{para: u["para"], text: u["text"], quoted: u["quoted"]} end)
    end
  end
end

defmodule ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.Text do
  @moduledoc """
  Chapter HTML to paragraphs, and paragraphs to quote-level units: a quotation
  is its own unit, so the narration around it and the speech in it can be read
  from different clips.
  """

  # Their bodies are code, not prose (an ad <script> was once read aloud).
  @opaque_blocks ~r/<(script|style|iframe)\b[^>]*>.*?<\/\1\s*>/is
  @breaks ~r/<\s*br\s*\/?>|<\/\s*(p|div|h\d|li)\s*>/i
  @header ~r/^\s*(Translator|Editor|Proofreader)\s*:/i

  to standard Mandarin ("Feng Jiu Ge" → "Fung Jyo Guhh"), and the substitution of

  @spec respell(String.t()) :: String.t() | nil
  def respell(name) do

      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace("v", "ü")
      |> String.split()

    spelled =
      Enum.map(words, fn word ->
        case parse(String.graphemes(word)) do
          nil -> nil
          syllables -> syllables |> Enum.map_join(&syllable/1) |> capitalize()
        end

  end

  names apply to the whole book, and a one-word name ("Long", "Men") is too often
  an English word: respelling it would change ordinary prose.
  """
  @spec new_names([String.t()], String.t(), map()) :: %{String.t() => String.t()}
  def new_names(found, text, known) do
    for name <- Enum.map(found, &String.trim/1),
        String.contains?(name, " "),
        not Map.has_key?(known, name),
        String.contains?(text, name),
        spelled = respell(name),
        spelled != nil,
        into: %{},
        do: {name, spelled}
  end

  and match exactly; lowercase keys are word fixes ("feathermen" → "feather men")
  that match in any case and keep a leading capital.
  """

  def apply(text, mapping) when map_size(mapping) == 0, do: text

  def apply(text, mapping) do
    alternatives =
      mapping
      |> Map.keys()
      |> Enum.sort_by(&(-String.length(&1)))
      |> Enum.map_join("|", fn key ->
        if key == String.downcase(key),
          do: "(?i:#{Regex.escape(key)})",
          else: Regex.escape(key)
      end)

    pattern = Regex.compile!("\\b(" <> alternatives <> ")\\b", "u")

    Regex.replace(pattern, text, fn found, _ ->
      case Map.fetch(mapping, found) do
        {:ok, replacement} ->
          replacement

        :error ->
          fix = Map.fetch!(mapping, String.downcase(found))
          if upper?(String.first(found)), do: capitalize(fix), else: fix
      end
    end)
  end

  defp parse([]), do: []

  defp parse(graphemes) do
    min(6, length(graphemes))..1//-1
    |> Enum.find_value(fn n ->
      {head, rest} = Enum.split(graphemes, n)
      head = Enum.join(head)

      with spelled when spelled != nil <- syllable(head),
           parsed when parsed != nil <- parse(rest) do
        [head | parsed]
      else
        _ -> nil
      end
    end)
  end

  defp syllable(syl) do
    case Map.fetch(@whole, syl) do
      {:ok, spelled} -> spelled
      :error -> initial_final(syl)
    end
  end

  defp initial_final(syl) do
    case Enum.find(@initials_longest_first, &String.starts_with?(syl, &1)) do
      nil ->
        nil

      ini ->
        fin = String.replace_prefix(syl, ini, "")

        cond do
          fin == "i" and Map.has_key?(@apical, ini) -> @initials[ini] <> @apical[ini]
          ini in ["j", "q", "x"] and Map.has_key?(@jqx_finals, fin) -> @initials[ini] <> @jqx_finals[fin]
          Map.has_key?(@finals, fin) -> @initials[ini] <> @finals[fin]
          true -> nil
        end
    end
  end

  defp capitalize(word) do
    {first, rest} = String.split_at(word, 1)
    String.upcase(first) <> rest
  end

  defp upper?(nil), do: false
  defp upper?(char), do: char != String.downcase(char)
end

defmodule ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.Text do
  @moduledoc """
  Chapter HTML to paragraphs, and paragraphs to quote-level units: a quotation
  is its own unit, so the narration around it and the speech in it can be read
  from different clips.
  """

  # Their bodies are code, not prose (an ad <script> was once read aloud).
  @opaque_blocks ~r/<(script|style|iframe)\b[^>]*>.*?<\/\1\s*>/is
  @breaks ~r/<\s*br\s*\/?>|<\/\s*(p|div|h\d|li)\s*>/i
  @header ~r/^\s*(Translator|Editor|Proofreader)\s*:/i
  @entity ~r/&(#[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+|#\d+|[a-zA-Z]+);/

  @named %{
    "amp" => "&",
    "lt" => "<",
    "gt" => ">",
    "quot" => "\"",
    "apos" => "'",
    "nbsp" => "\u00A0",
    "lsquo" => "‘",
    "rsquo" => "’",
    "ldquo" => "“",
    "rdquo" => "”",
    "hellip" => "…",
    "mdash" => "—",
    "ndash" => "–",
    "middot" => "·",
    "bull" => "•",
    "laquo" => "«",
    "raquo" => "»"
  }

  @quote_close %{"“" => "”", "\"" => "\""}

  @doc "Non-empty paragraphs of a chapter, without translator/editor credit lines."
  @spec paragraphs(String.t()) :: [String.t()]
  def paragraphs(html) do
    html
    |> String.replace(@opaque_blocks, " ")
    |> String.replace(@breaks, "\n")
    |> String.replace(~r/<[^>]+>/, "")
    |> unescape()
    |> String.split("\n")
    |> Enum.map(&String.trim/1)
    |> Enum.reject(&(&1 == "" or Regex.match?(@header, &1)))
  end

  @doc """
  Each paragraph cut into quoted and unquoted runs, in order; they rejoin to the
  paragraph exactly. An unclosed quote runs to the end of its paragraph.
  """
  @spec units([String.t()]) :: [%{para: non_neg_integer(), text: String.t(), quoted: boolean()}]
  def units(paragraphs) do
    paragraphs
    |> Enum.with_index()
    |> Enum.flat_map(fn {para, p} ->
      para |> split_quotes([]) |> Enum.map(fn {text, quoted} -> %{para: p, text: text, quoted: quoted} end)
    end)
  end

  defp split_quotes("", acc), do: Enum.reverse(acc)

  defp split_quotes(rest, acc) do
    case :binary.match(rest, Map.keys(@quote_close)) do
      :nomatch ->
        Enum.reverse([{rest, false} | acc])

      {start, len} ->
        open = binary_part(rest, start, len)
        acc = if start > 0, do: [{binary_part(rest, 0, start), false} | acc], else: acc
        after_open = binary_part(rest, start + len, byte_size(rest) - start - len)

        {quoted, rest} =
          case :binary.match(after_open, @quote_close[open]) do
            :nomatch ->
              {open <> after_open, ""}

            {close, clen} ->
              {open <> binary_part(after_open, 0, close + clen),
               binary_part(after_open, close + clen, byte_size(after_open) - close - clen)}
          end

        split_quotes(rest, [{quoted, true} | acc])
    end
  end

  defp unescape(text) do
    Regex.replace(@entity, text, fn whole, entity ->
      case entity do
        "#x" <> hex -> codepoint(Integer.parse(hex, 16), whole)
        "#X" <> hex -> codepoint(Integer.parse(hex, 16), whole)
        "#" <> dec -> codepoint(Integer.parse(dec), whole)
        name -> Map.get(@named, name, whole)
      end
    end)
  end

  defp codepoint({cp, ""}, _whole) when cp in 1..0xD7FF or cp in 0xE000..0x10FFFF, do: <<cp::utf8>>
  defp codepoint(_, whole), do: whole
end

defmodule ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.BonsaiTest do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true

  alias ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.Bonsai

  # A fake model that answers each request with `reply.(lines_marked_tag)`.
  defp model(reply) do
    me = self()

    fn system, user, schema ->
      send(me, {:asked, system, user, schema})
      tagged = for line <- String.split(user, "\n"), [_, i] <- [Regex.run(~r/^\[(\d+)\] TAG:/, line)], do: String.to_integer(i)
      reply.(tagged)
    end
  end

  defp tags_for(ids), do: {:ok, %{"tags" => Enum.map(ids, &%{"i" => &1, "kind" => "dialogue", "speaker" => "Fang Yuan", "sex" => "male", "mood" => "calm"})}}

  test "labels in windows of 40 with neighbouring lines as context" do
    texts = Enum.map(0..84, &"line #{&1}")
    tags = Bonsai.tag(model(&tags_for/1), texts, "A novel.")
    assert length(tags) == 85
    assert Enum.all?(tags, &(&1.speaker == "Fang Yuan"))

    assert_received {:asked, system, user1, _}
    assert system =~ "A novel."
    refute user1 =~ "[39] CONTEXT"
    assert user1 =~ "[40] CONTEXT: line 40"
    assert_received {:asked, _, user2, _}
    assert user2 =~ "[35] CONTEXT: line 35"
    assert user2 =~ "[40] TAG: line 40"
  end

  test "a window whose reply misses lines is asked again" do
    {:ok, calls} = Agent.start_link(fn -> 0 end)

    reply = fn ids ->
      n = Agent.get_and_update(calls, &{&1, &1 + 1})
      if n == 0, do: tags_for(Enum.take(ids, 1)), else: tags_for(ids)
    end

    tags = Bonsai.tag(model(reply), ["a", "b", "c"], "ctx")
    assert Enum.all?(tags, &(&1.kind == "dialogue"))
    assert Agent.get(calls, & &1) == 2
  end

  test "lines still missing after the retry are read as narration" do
    tags = Bonsai.tag(model(fn _ -> {:error, :truncated} end), ["a", "b"], "ctx")
    assert Enum.all?(tags, &(&1 == %{kind: "narration", speaker: "narrator", sex: "unknown", mood: "calm"}))
  end

  test "assign offers only the menu's voice ids" do
    reply = fn ids -> {:ok, %{"picks" => Enum.map(ids, &%{"i" => &1, "cluster" => "male-0"})}} end
    assert Bonsai.assign(model(reply), ["a"], %{"male-0" => "male, casual", "female-0" => "female, warm"}, "ctx") == ["male-0"]
    assert_received {:asked, system, _, schema}
    assert system =~ "- female-0: female, warm"
    assert schema.properties.picks.items.properties.cluster.enum == ["female-0", "male-0"]
  end

  test "names retries a bad reply once, then gives up quietly" do
    {:ok, calls} = Agent.start_link(fn -> 0 end)

    flaky = fn _, _, _ ->
      if Agent.get_and_update(calls, &{&1, &1 + 1}) == 0, do: {:error, :truncated}, else: {:ok, %{"names" => ["Bo Qing"]}}
    end

    assert Bonsai.names(flaky, "text") == ["Bo Qing"]
    assert Bonsai.names(fn _, _, _ -> {:error, :truncated} end, "text") == []
  end
end
EOF

defmodule ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.LibraryTest do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true

  alias ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.Library

  @lib %Library{
    model: "breeze-tts-2",
    voice: "heath-miller",
    temperature: 0.6,
    fallback: %{voice: "/models/voices/heath-miller.wav", text: "The walls were black."},
    voices: %{
      "female-0" => %{group: "female", size: 48, label: "female, warm", sex: "female", description: "Warm.", clip: %{voice: "/models/voices/f0.wav", text: "F0."}},
      "female-1" => %{group: "female", size: 46, label: "female, expressive", sex: "female", description: "Wide.", clip: %{voice: "/models/voices/f1.wav", text: "F1."}},
      "male-0" => %{group: "male", size: 235, label: "male, casual", sex: "male", description: "Casual.", clip: %{voice: "/models/voices/m0.wav", text: "M0."}},
      "male-2" => %{group: "male", size: 167, label: "male, serious", sex: "male", description: "Serious.", clip: %{voice: "/models/voices/m2.wav", text: "M2."}},
      "narration-0" => %{group: "narration", size: 401, label: "narration, calm", sex: "male", description: "Calm.", clip: %{voice: "/models/voices/n0.wav", text: "N0."}}
    }
  }

  defp dialogue(speaker, sex), do: %{kind: "dialogue", speaker: speaker, sex: sex, mood: "calm"}
  @narration %{kind: "narration", speaker: "narrator", sex: "unknown", mood: "calm"}

  test "the shipped library for the cloned narrator loads" do
    assert {:ok, lib} = Library.for_voice(%ReadaloudTTS.Voice{model: "breeze-tts-2", voice: "heath-miller"})
    assert lib.temperature == 0.6
    assert Enum.any?(lib.voices, fn {_, v} -> v.group == "female" end)
    assert Library.for_voice(%ReadaloudTTS.Voice{model: "kokoro", voice: "af_heart"}) == :none
  end

  test "the menu describes each voice for the model" do
    assert Library.menu(@lib)["female-0"] == "female, warm (female): Warm."
  end

  describe "enforce_group/3" do
    test "a woman's line never gets a man's voice, and dialogue never a narration voice" do
      tags = [dialogue("Hei Lou Lan", "female"), dialogue("Fang Yuan", "male"), @narration]
      picks = Library.enforce_group(@lib, tags, ["male-0", "narration-0", "female-0"])
      # Wrong group: the group's largest voice instead.
      assert picks == ["female-0", "male-0", "narration-0"]
    end

    test "speakers of unknown sex all get the default male voice" do
      assert Library.enforce_group(@lib, [dialogue("Self Gu", "unknown")], ["male-2"]) == ["male-0"]
    end

    test "a right-group pick stands" do
      assert Library.enforce_group(@lib, [dialogue("Mother", "female")], ["female-1"]) == ["female-1"]
    end
  end

  test "one voice per speaker: the voice picked most often for them" do
    tags = [dialogue("Fang Yuan", "male"), dialogue("Fang Yuan", "male"), dialogue("Fang Yuan", "male"), @narration]
    assert Library.one_voice_per_speaker(tags, ["male-0", "male-2", "male-2", "narration-0"]) ==
             ["male-2", "male-2", "male-2", "narration-0"]
  end

  describe "remember_speakers/4" do
    test "characters keep their voice across chapters" do
      tags = [dialogue("Fang Yuan", "male"), dialogue("Bai Ning Bing", "male"), @narration]
      {picks, memory} = Library.remember_speakers(@lib, tags, ["male-0", "male-0", "narration-0"], %{"Fang Yuan" => "male-2"})
      assert picks == ["male-2", "male-0", "narration-0"]
      assert memory == %{"Fang Yuan" => "male-2", "Bai Ning Bing" => "male-0"}
    end

    test "a remembered voice of the wrong group is replaced" do
      {picks, memory} = Library.remember_speakers(@lib, [dialogue("Gu", "female")], ["female-0"], %{"Gu" => "male-0"})
      assert picks == ["female-0"]
      assert memory == %{"Gu" => "female-0"}
    end
  end

  test "clip/2 falls back to the voice's own clip for no pick" do
    assert Library.clip(@lib, "female-0") == %{voice: "/models/voices/f0.wav", text: "F0."}
    assert Library.clip(@lib, nil) == @lib.fallback
  end
end

defmodule ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.PassagesTest do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true

  alias ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.Passages

  @narr %{kind: "narration", speaker: "narrator", sex: "unknown", mood: "calm"}
  @her %{kind: "dialogue", speaker: "Hei Lou Lan", sex: "female", mood: "intense"}
  @n %{voice: "/models/voices/n0.wav", text: "N0."}
  @f %{voice: "/models/voices/f0.wav", text: "F0."}

  defp unit(para, text), do: %{para: para, text: text, quoted: false}

  describe "build/2" do
    test "one passage per speaker turn; calm narration across paragraphs merges" do
      units = [unit(0, "He walked in. "), unit(0, "“Leave,”"), unit(0, " she said."), unit(1, "The hall was cold.")]
      passages = Passages.build(units, [@narr, @her, @narr, @narr])
      assert Enum.map(passages, & &1.text) == ["He walked in. ", "“Leave,”", " she said.\nThe hall was cold."]
    end

    test "narration stops merging at 800 characters" do
      long = String.duplicate("a", 500)
      passages = Passages.build([unit(0, long), unit(1, long)], [@narr, @narr])
      assert length(passages) == 2
    end
  end

  describe "chunks/2" do
    test "each chunk has the book's text, the spoken text and its clip" do
      chunks = Passages.chunks([{"Feng Jiu Ge smiled.", @n}], %{"Feng Jiu Ge" => "Fung Jyo Guhh"})

      assert chunks == [
               %{"text" => "Feng Jiu Ge smiled.", "spoken" => "Fung Jyo Guhh smiled.", "voice" => @n.voice, "reference_text" => "N0."}
             ]
    end

    test "neighbours with the same clip share a request up to 400 characters" do
      chunks = Passages.chunks([{"He walked in.", @n}, {"The hall was cold.", @n}, {"“Leave.”", @f}, {"She turned.", @n}], %{})
      assert Enum.map(chunks, & &1["text"]) == ["He walked in.\nThe hall was cold.", "“Leave.”", "She turned."]
    end

    test "long passages are cut at 400 characters and nothing is lost" do
      text = String.trim(String.duplicate("Fang Yuan nodded slowly. ", 40))
      chunks = Passages.chunks([{text, @n}], %{})
      assert length(chunks) > 1
      assert Enum.all?(chunks, &(String.length(&1["spoken"]) <= 400))
      assert Enum.map_join(chunks, " ", & &1["text"]) == text
    end

    test "a piece with no words joins its neighbour (Breeze can fail on it)" do
      chunks = Passages.chunks([{"“Leave.”", @f}, {"***", @n}, {"“Now.”", @f}], %{})
      assert Enum.map(chunks, & &1["text"]) == ["“Leave.”\n***", "“Now.”"]

      chunks = Passages.chunks([{"……", @n}, {"“Leave.”", @f}], %{})
      assert Enum.map(chunks, & &1["text"]) == ["……\n“Leave.”"]
    end
  end
end

defmodule ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.Library do
  @moduledoc """
  A cloned narrator's voices: the registers he reads in (narration, women's and
  men's voices of several temperaments), each with the clip of him it is read from.

  Found by clustering his audiobook in tools/voice-refs and exported to
  `priv/voice_libraries/<model>--<voice>.json` (`voicerefs export-library`). A
  voice with no library is read from its single clip, as before.
  """

  @enforce_keys [:model, :voice, :voices, :fallback]
  defstruct [:model, :voice, :temperature, :fallback, :voices]

  @type clip :: %{voice: String.t(), text: String.t()}
  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          model: String.t(),
          voice: String.t(),
          temperature: float() | nil,
          fallback: clip(),
          voices: %{String.t() => map()}
        }

  @spec for_voice(ReadaloudTTS.Voice.t()) :: {:ok, t()} | :none
  def for_voice(%ReadaloudTTS.Voice{model: model, voice: voice}) do
    path = Path.join([:code.priv_dir(:readaloud_audiobook), "voice_libraries", "#{model}--#{voice}.json"])

    case File.read(path) do
      {:ok, json} -> {:ok, json |> Jason.decode!() |> from_json()}
      {:error, :enoent} -> :none
    end
  end

  defp from_json(map) do
    %__MODULE__{
      model: map["model"],
      voice: map["voice"],
      temperature: map["temperature"],
      fallback: clip_from(map["fallback"]),
      voices:
        Map.new(map["voices"], fn {id, v} ->
          {id,
           %{
             label: v["label"],
             sex: v["sex"],
             description: v["description"],
             group: v["group"],
             size: v["size"],
             clip: clip_from(v["clip"])
           }}
        end)
    }
  end

  defp clip_from(%{"voice" => voice, "text" => text}), do: %{voice: voice, text: text}

  @doc "What the model is told about each voice when choosing one per line."
  def menu(%__MODULE__{voices: voices}) do
    Map.new(voices, fn {id, v} -> {id, "#{v.label} (#{v.sex}): #{v.description}"} end)
  end

  @doc "The clip a passage is read from; no pick reads from the voice's own clip."
  def clip(%__MODULE__{voices: voices, fallback: fallback}, id) do
    case Map.fetch(voices, id || "") do
      {:ok, v} -> v.clip
      :error -> fallback
    end
  end

defmodule ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.Passages do
  @moduledoc """
  Tagged units to passages (one per speaker turn), and passages with their clips
  to the chunks of a voice plan.
  """

  alias ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.Names
  alias ReadaloudTTS.TextChunker

  @max_narration 800
  @max_chars 400

  @doc """
  One passage per speaker turn: a unit joins the passage before it when the tag is
  the same and it is in the same paragraph, or it is calm-enough narration that the
  passage stays under #{@max_narration} characters.
  """
  def build(units, tags) do
    units
    |> Enum.zip(tags)
    |> Enum.reduce({[], nil}, fn {unit, tag}, {passages, last_para} ->
      case passages do
        [%{tag: ^tag} = prev | rest] when unit.para == last_para ->
          {[%{prev | text: prev.text <> unit.text} | rest], unit.para}

        [%{tag: ^tag} = prev | rest]
        when tag.kind == "narration" and
               byte_size(prev.text) + byte_size(unit.text) + 1 <= @max_narration * 4 ->
          if String.length(prev.text) + String.length(unit.text) + 1 <= @max_narration do
            {[%{prev | text: prev.text <> "\n" <> unit.text} | rest], unit.para}
          else
            {[%{text: unit.text, tag: tag} | passages], unit.para}
          end

        _ ->
          {[%{text: unit.text, tag: tag} | passages], unit.para}
      end
    end)
    |> elem(0)
    |> Enum.reverse()
  end

  @doc """
  Plan chunks from `{passage_text, clip}` pairs in reading order: neighbours with the
  same clip share one request up to #{@max_chars} characters, cut like readaloud
  cuts text, and a piece with no words joins a neighbour.
  """
  def chunks(passages, name_map) do
    passages
    |> Enum.map(fn {text, clip} -> {String.trim(text), clip} end)
    |> Enum.reject(fn {text, _} -> text == "" end)
    |> Enum.reduce([], fn {text, clip}, runs ->
      case runs do
        [{^clip, prev} | rest] when byte_size(prev) >= 0 ->
          if String.length(prev) + 1 + String.length(text) <= @max_chars,
            do: [{clip, prev <> "\n" <> text} | rest],
            else: [{clip, text} | runs]

        _ ->
          [{clip, text} | runs]
      end
    end)
    |> Enum.reverse()
    |> Enum.flat_map(fn {clip, text} -> Enum.map(TextChunker.chunk(text, @max_chars), &{clip, &1}) end)
    |> fold_wordless()
    |> Enum.map(fn {clip, piece} ->
      %{"text" => piece, "spoken" => Names.apply(piece, name_map), "voice" => clip.voice, "reference_text" => clip.text}
    end)
  end

  # Breeze can fail on a request with nothing to say ("***", a silent "……").
  defp fold_wordless(pieces) do
    {out, pending} =
      Enum.reduce(pieces, {[], ""}, fn {clip, text}, {out, pending} ->
        cond do
          Regex.match?(~r/\w/u, text) -> {[{clip, pending <> text} | out], ""}
          out == [] -> {out, pending <> text <> "\n"}
          true -> {[{elem(hd(out), 0), elem(hd(out), 1) <> "\n" <> text} | tl(out)], pending}
        end
      end)

    if pending == "", do: Enum.reverse(out), else: Enum.reverse(out)
  end
end

    Map.new(voices, fn {id, v} -> {id, "#{v.label} (#{v.sex}): #{v.description}"} end)
  end

  @doc "The clip a passage is read from; no pick reads from the voice's own clip."
  def clip(%__MODULE__{voices: voices, fallback: fallback}, id) do
    case Map.fetch(voices, id || "") do
      {:ok, v} -> v.clip
      :error -> fallback
    end
  end

  @doc """
  A passage's voice must come from its own group: a woman's line never gets a man's
  voice, and dialogue never a narration voice. A wrong pick becomes the group's
  largest voice; speakers of unknown sex (Gu worms) all get the largest male voice.
  """
  def enforce_group(%__MODULE__{voices: voices}, tags, picks) do
    Enum.zip_with(tags, picks, fn tag, pick ->
      want =
        cond do
          tag.kind == "narration" -> "narration"
          tag.sex == "female" -> "female"
          true -> "male"
        end

      unknown_sex? = tag.kind == "dialogue" and tag.sex not in ["female", "male"]

      if pick != nil and get_in(voices, [pick, :group]) == want and not unknown_sex? do
        pick
      else
        voices
        |> Enum.filter(fn {_, v} -> v.group == want end)
        |> Enum.max_by(fn {_, v} -> v.size end, fn -> {nil, nil} end)
        |> elem(0)
      end
    end)
  end

  @doc "Each character keeps the voice picked most often for them in the chapter."
  def one_voice_per_speaker(tags, picks) do
    votes =
      Enum.zip(tags, picks)
      |> Enum.filter(fn {t, p} -> t.kind == "dialogue" and p != nil end)
      |> Enum.group_by(fn {t, _} -> t.speaker end, fn {_, p} -> p end)
      |> Map.new(fn {speaker, ps} ->
        # Ties go to the voice picked first, as Python's Counter.most_common does.
        freq = Enum.frequencies(ps)
        {speaker, Enum.max_by(Enum.uniq(ps), &freq[&1])}
      end)

    Enum.zip_with(tags, picks, fn t, p ->
      if t.kind == "dialogue", do: Map.get(votes, t.speaker, p), else: p
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Characters keep the voice they were first given, across chapters, while it is of
  the right group. Returns the picks and the updated speaker => voice memory.
  """
  def remember_speakers(%__MODULE__{voices: voices}, tags, picks, memory) do
    Enum.zip(tags, picks)
    |> Enum.map_reduce(memory, fn {tag, pick}, memory ->
      kept = Map.get(memory, tag.speaker)

      cond do
        tag.kind != "dialogue" or pick == nil -> {pick, memory}
        kept != nil and get_in(voices, [kept, :group]) == get_in(voices, [pick, :group]) -> {kept, memory}
        true -> {pick, Map.put(memory, tag.speaker, pick)}
      end
    end)
  end
end

defmodule ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.Passages do
  @moduledoc """
  Tagged units to passages (one per speaker turn), and passages with their clips
  to the chunks of a voice plan.
  """

  alias ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.Names
  alias ReadaloudTTS.TextChunker

  @max_narration 800
  @max_chars 400

  @doc """
  One passage per speaker turn: a unit joins the passage before it when the tag is
  the same and it is in the same paragraph, or it is calm-enough narration that the
  passage stays under #{@max_narration} characters.
  """
  def build(units, tags) do
    units
    |> Enum.zip(tags)
    |> Enum.reduce({[], nil}, fn {unit, tag}, {passages, last_para} ->
      case passages do
        [%{tag: ^tag} = prev | rest] when unit.para == last_para ->
          {[%{prev | text: prev.text <> unit.text} | rest], unit.para}

        [%{tag: ^tag} = prev | rest]
        when tag.kind == "narration" and
               byte_size(prev.text) + byte_size(unit.text) + 1 <= @max_narration * 4 ->
          if String.length(prev.text) + String.length(unit.text) + 1 <= @max_narration do
            {[%{prev | text: prev.text <> "\n" <> unit.text} | rest], unit.para}
          else
            {[%{text: unit.text, tag: tag} | passages], unit.para}
          end

        _ ->
          {[%{text: unit.text, tag: tag} | passages], unit.para}
      end
    end)
    |> elem(0)
    |> Enum.reverse()
  end

  @doc """
  Plan chunks from `{passage_text, clip}` pairs in reading order: neighbours with the
  same clip share one request up to #{@max_chars} characters, cut like readaloud
  cuts text, and a piece with no words joins a neighbour.
  """
  def chunks(passages, name_map) do
    passages
    |> Enum.map(fn {text, clip} -> {String.trim(text), clip} end)
    |> Enum.reject(fn {text, _} -> text == "" end)
    |> Enum.reduce([], fn {text, clip}, runs ->
      case runs do
        [{^clip, prev} | rest] when byte_size(prev) >= 0 ->
          if String.length(prev) + 1 + String.length(text) <= @max_chars,
            do: [{clip, prev <> "\n" <> text} | rest],
            else: [{clip, text} | runs]

        _ ->
          [{clip, text} | runs]
      end
    end)
    |> Enum.reverse()
    |> Enum.flat_map(fn {clip, text} -> Enum.map(TextChunker.chunk(text, @max_chars), &{clip, &1}) end)
    |> fold_wordless()
    |> Enum.map(fn {clip, piece} ->
      %{"text" => piece, "spoken" => Names.apply(piece, name_map), "voice" => clip.voice, "reference_text" => clip.text}
    end)
  end

  # Breeze can fail on a request with nothing to say ("***", a silent "……").
  defp fold_wordless(pieces) do
    {out, pending} =
      Enum.reduce(pieces, {[], ""}, fn {clip, text}, {out, pending} ->
        cond do
          Regex.match?(~r/\w/u, text) -> {[{clip, pending <> text} | out], ""}
          out == [] -> {out, pending <> text <> "\n"}
          true -> {[{elem(hd(out), 0), elem(hd(out), 1) <> "\n" <> text} | tl(out)], pending}
        end
      end)

    if pending == "", do: Enum.reverse(out), else: Enum.reverse(out)
  end
end

Chapter 959: Duel

Translator: Atlas Studios

Feng Jiu Ge smiled. “Leave,” Hei Lou Lan said.

“Never,” Fang Yuan replied.

""" # A fake Bonsai: tags quotes by who is named in them, picks voices by sex, names Feng Jiu Ge. def model(texts_seen \\ self()) do fn _system, user, schema -> send(texts_seen, {:asked, Map.keys(schema.properties)}) lines = for l <- String.split(user, "\n"), [_, i, t] <- [Regex.run(~r/^\[(\d+)\] TAG: (.*)$/, l)], do: {String.to_integer(i), t} case Map.keys(schema.properties) do [:tags] -> {:ok, %{"tags" => Enum.map(lines, fn {i, t} -> tag(i, t) end)}} [:picks] -> {:ok, %{"picks" => Enum.map(lines, fn {i, t} -> %{"i" => i, "cluster" => if(t =~ "Leave", do: "female-0", else: defmodule ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner do
  @moduledoc """
  Makes a chapter's voice plan (`ReadaloudAudiobook.VoicePlan`) for a cloned
  narrator with a voice library (`Planner.Library`): the chapter is cut into speaker
  turns, the language model (`Planner.Bonsai`) says who speaks each one and which of
  the narrator's voices fits it, and names are respelled so the voice says them
  right. A woman's line is then read from a clip of him voicing a woman, and so on.

  This is the pipeline Noah approved on the voice-refs comparison page
  (tools/voice-refs, Oct 2026), minus laya: Bonsai's own mood tag covers it.
  """

  alias ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner.{Bonsai, Library, Names, Passages, State, Text}
  alias ReadaloudAudiobook.VoicePlan

  require Logger

  @doc """
  Plans and saves a chapter for `voice`. `:none` when the voice has no library or no
  model is configured (`BONSAI_URL`); the chapter is then read from the voice's own clip.

  Options: `chat` (a `Planner.Bonsai` chat function; nil for none), `base` (storage root).
  """
  @spec plan_chapter(map(), ReadaloudTTS.Voice.t(), keyword()) :: {:ok, VoicePlan.t()} | :none | {:error, term()}
  def plan_chapter(chapter, voice, opts \\ []) do
    base = Keyword.get(opts, :base, System.get_env("STORAGE_PATH", "priv/static/files"))
    chat = Keyword.get_lazy(opts, :chat, &default_chat/0)

    with {:ok, library} <- Library.for_voice(voice),
         true <- chat != nil || :none,
         {:ok, html} <- ReadaloudLibrary.get_chapter_content(chapter) do
      book = ReadaloudLibrary.get_book!(chapter.book_id)
      state = State.load(book.id, base, State.new(book.title))
      started = System.monotonic_time(:millisecond)

      with {:ok, doc, state} <- plan(html, library, state, chat),
           {:ok, plan} <- VoicePlan.save(chapter, doc, base) do
        State.save(state, book.id, base)
        Logger.info("Planned chapter #{chapter.number}: #{length(plan.chunks)} chunks in #{System.monotonic_time(:millisecond) - started} ms")
        {:ok, plan}
      end
    end
  end

  defp default_chat do
    case System.get_env("BONSAI_URL") do
      url when url in [nil, ""] -> nil
      url -> Bonsai.chat(url)
    end
  end

  @doc "The plan document for one chapter's HTML, and the book's state after it."
  @spec plan(String.t(), Library.t(), State.t(), function()) :: {:ok, map(), State.t()} | {:error, term()}
  def plan(html, %Library{} = library, %State{} = state, chat) do
    paragraphs = Text.paragraphs(html)
    units = Text.units(paragraphs)

    if units == [] do
      {:error, :empty_chapter}
    else
      context = state.context || ""
      tags = Bonsai.tag(chat, Enum.map(units, & &1.text), context)
      passages = Passages.build(units, tags)
      passage_tags = Enum.map(passages, & &1.tag)

      picks =
        chat
        |> Bonsai.assign(Enum.map(passages, &String.trim(&1.text)), Library.menu(library), context)

defmodule ReadaloudAudiobook.PlanJob do
  @moduledoc """
  Plans a chapter's voice (`ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner`) ahead of its generation
  job, on its own queue: planning waits on the language model, so doing it here
  keeps the TTS queue reading while the next chapters are planned. A generation job
  that gets there first plans the chapter itself.
  """

  use Oban.Worker,
    queue: :plan,
    max_attempts: 2,
    unique: [keys: [:chapter_id, :model, :voice], states: [:available, :scheduled, :executing, :retryable]]

  alias ReadaloudAudiobook.{Planner, VoicePlan}
  alias ReadaloudTTS.Voice

  require Logger

  @impl Oban.Worker
  def perform(%Oban.Job{args: %{"chapter_id" => chapter_id, "model" => model, "voice" => voice}}) do
    chapter = ReadaloudLibrary.get_chapter!(chapter_id)
    voice = %Voice{model: model, voice: voice}

    case chapter |> VoicePlan.load() |> VoicePlan.for_voice(voice) do
      {:ok, _plan} ->
        :ok

      _ ->
        case Planner.plan_chapter(chapter, voice, Application.get_env(:readaloud_audiobook, :planner_opts, [])) do
          {:ok, _plan} -> :ok
          :none -> :ok
          {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason}
        end
    end
  end
end
EOF

defmodule ReadaloudAudiobook.PlanJob do
  @moduledoc """
  Plans a chapter's voice (`ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner`) ahead of its generation
  job, on its own queue: planning waits on the language model, so doing it here
  keeps the TTS queue reading while the next chapters are planned. A generation job
  that gets there first plans the chapter itself.
  """

  use Oban.Worker,
    queue: :plan,
    max_attempts: 2,
    unique: [keys: [:chapter_id, :model, :voice], states: [:available, :scheduled, :executing, :retryable]]

  alias ReadaloudAudiobook.{Planner, VoicePlan}
  alias ReadaloudTTS.Voice

  require Logger

  @impl Oban.Worker
  def perform(%Oban.Job{args: %{"chapter_id" => chapter_id, "model" => model, "voice" => voice}}) do
    chapter = ReadaloudLibrary.get_chapter!(chapter_id)
    voice = %Voice{model: model, voice: voice}

    case chapter |> VoicePlan.load() |> VoicePlan.for_voice(voice) do
      {:ok, _plan} ->
        :ok

      _ ->
        case Planner.plan_chapter(chapter, voice, Application.get_env(:readaloud_audiobook, :planner_opts, [])) do
          {:ok, _plan} -> :ok
          :none -> :ok
          {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason}
        end
    end
  end
end

def plan(html, %Library{} = library, %State{} = state, chat) do
    paragraphs = Text.paragraphs(html)
    units = Text.units(paragraphs)

    context = state.context || ""

    with false <- units == [] || {:error, :empty_chapter},
         {:ok, tags} <- Bonsai.tag(chat, Enum.map(units, & &1.text), context),
         passages = Passages.build(units, tags),
         {:ok, picks} <- Bonsai.assign(chat, Enum.map(passages, &String.trim(&1.text)), Library.menu(library), context) do
      passage_tags = Enum.map(passages, & &1.tag)

      picks =
        library
        |> Library.enforce_group(passage_tags, picks)
        |> then(&Library.one_voice_per_speaker(passage_tags, &1))

      {picks, speakers} = Library.remember_speakers(library, passage_tags, picks, state.speakers)

      text = Enum.join(paragraphs, "\n")
      known = Map.merge(state.names, state.words)
      names = Map.merge(Names.new_names(Bonsai.names(chat, text), text, known), state.names)
      name_map = Map.merge(names, state.words)

      chunks =
        passages
        |> Enum.zip(picks)
        |> Enum.map(fn {p, pick} -> {p.text, Library.clip(library, pick)} end)
        |> Passages.chunks(name_map)

      doc = %{"model" => library.model, "voice" => library.voice, "temperature" => library.temperature, "chunks" => chunks}
      {:ok, doc, %{state | names: names, speakers: speakers}}
    end
  end

feat(audiobook): plan chapter voices inside readaloud

The per-chapter voice planner moves from tools/voice-refs into readaloud
(ReadaloudAudiobook.Planner): chapter text is cut into speaker turns,
Bonsai (BONSAI_URL, the resident server shared with the gameassets tagger)
tags who speaks each and picks one of the narrator's voices, and names are
respelled. The narrator's voice library ships in priv/voice_libraries
(exported by `voicerefs export-library`); per-book learned names, word
fixes and character voices are kept beside the plans.

GenerateJob plans a chapter that has no plan, falling back to the voice's
own clip if planning fails; PlanJob plans ahead on its own :plan queue,
queued with every generation job for a voice that has a library. Laya is
dropped: Bonsai's mood tag covers it. Respelling and text splitting are
tested against fixtures from the Python implementation.
